---
title: "Capstone: Final Group Presentation"
---

The final for this class is a **group presentation (5–10 minutes)** exploring
a plant genetics topic of your group's choice, presented in class on
**December 1 and 3**. Groups are 4–5 people. It's worth 30% of your grade
(100 points, plus up to 5 extra credit).

## Start thinking about it now

The capstone comes at the end, but the best presentations start much
earlier — in two ways.

**The topic.** Ideas will come at you all quarter: a lecture that hooks you,
a reading, the cacao tour, a guest speaker, something you dig up researching
your midterm. When something makes you think "I want to know more about
that," write it down — that list is where good capstone topics come from.
Like the midterm, focused beats broad, and the same three doors apply: a
problem plant genetics can help solve, an open question, or how a genetic
technology works.

**The group.** This is a group project, which makes the class itself part of
the assignment: sit next to someone new, talk during the break, compare
answers during in-class activities. The people you meet in the first weeks
may well become your group — and groups that form around a shared interest
tend to have more fun with this. If you'd rather be assigned to a group,
that's completely fine too; the preference survey (due **Thu Oct 29**) asks
which you want.

## Timeline

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Thu **Oct 29**, 3:10 PM | **Group preference survey** on Canvas: form your own group (4–5 people) or ask to be assigned, plus topics you're interested in |
| Early Nov | Groups posted |
| Tue **Nov 17**, 3:10 PM | **Check-in #1** (part of "Quiz 7"): group members, topic, one useful citation, and what you personally plan to contribute |
| Tue **Nov 24** | No class meeting — the block is yours for group work. **Check-in #2** due 3:10 PM: bullet summary of your planned slides, and anything you're stuck on |
| Tue **Dec 1**, 3:10 PM | **ALL groups** (both presentation days): presentation file uploaded to Canvas (PDF or PPTX, one upload per group) + each student's individual contributions statement |
| Tue **Dec 1** + Thu **Dec 3** | Presentations in class |

## What you submit

- **Presentation file** (PDF or PPTX) — one upload per group on Canvas;
  anyone in the group can submit and it counts for everyone. Due Dec 1 at
  3:10 PM regardless of which day your group presents.
- **Individual contributions statement** — every student submits their own
  short, confidential statement: what you contributed (slides, research,
  figures, organizing, presenting sections…) and how the work was divided.
  A few sentences is plenty. Only the teaching team sees it; it's how we
  make sure credit lands where the work happened.

## How it's graded

The full rubric is attached to the Canvas assignment. The group grade covers
depth of content, accuracy, use of references (**at least 5 citations** on
your slides), introduction / body / conclusion structure, clarity, slide
design, collaboration, and time management (stay in the 5–10 minute window).
Two pieces are graded per student: your **individual contribution** (from
your statement) and **audience engagement** — being present and engaged
during the other groups' presentations, including asking at least one
thoughtful question across the two days. Up to 5 extra credit points for
genuinely creative insights or framings.
